chunks: Eavesdropping for telling lies, earning through unlawful means! So, if they come to you, judge between them or decline. And if you decline, they can do you no harm; but if you judge, you should do so with justice, for God loves those who are just.

key_terms.لِلْسُّحْتِ: unlawful earnings or food obtained by consuming people's wealth unjustly

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'suh't' in this verse and what choice does God give the Prophet regarding judging the hypocrites?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the incident of the Banu al-Sali' or the hypocrites who brought their disputes to the Prophet to seek his validation, highlighting the tension between political pragmatism and spiritual integrity. The command to judge with 'al-qist' (equity/justice) is interpreted not merely as legal fairness but as a divine mandate to uphold truth even against one's own interests, reinforcing the Imamate's role as the ultimate arbiter of justice. This passage underscores the Prophet's autonomy in choosing between engaging with the hypocrites' superficial compliance or withdrawing to preserve the purity of the message.
